newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN aid will have no EMU effect -Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: GAN aid will have no EMU effect -Arthuis.

text.p: The French government rescue plan for troubled state insurer GAN will have no state budget impact and no bearing on France's financial preparations for European economic and monetary union, finance minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday.
"This will not affect the state budget," Arthuis told a news conference.

"It has no Maastricht impact," he said, referring to the Maastricht treaty criteria calling on European Union states to keep public deficits to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year to join a single Euro currency in 1999.
Arthuis had just announced a rescue package for Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) which will cost up to 20 billion francs in total. Of that, 11 billion will be handed out in 1997.
Officials said there would be ample resources to pay for the rescue from privatisation receipts.

They said there was more than 10 billion francs in receipts left over from last year and also pointed to the planned sale of a stake in France Telecom this year, expected to raise at least 25 billion francs.
Another bailout, for state bank Credit Lyonnais was unlikely to incur much in the way of payouts from those privatisation funds in 1997, they added.
